TEXT
Climate change is no longer a distant threat for Tunisia: farmers report shorter rainy seasons, coastal towns face rising sea levels, and summers grow hotter each year. Adapting to these changes will not be easy, but it is not impossible either. Engineers have already designed more efficient irrigation systems that use far less water, while some coastal municipalities have begun building barriers to slow erosion. Scientists insist that these local efforts, though useful, must be matched by national policies: stricter water management, support for drought-resistant crops, and long-term investment in renewable energy. Without such coordinated action, they warn, the most vulnerable regions will suffer the most.

I. READING COMPREHENSION (6 marks)
1) According to the text, how is climate change already affecting Tunisia?   (2 marks)
2) What examples of local adaptation are mentioned?   (2 marks)
3) According to scientists, what is still missing to face the problem properly?   (2 marks)

II. TEXT ANALYSIS (4 marks)
1) State the main idea of the text in one sentence.   (2 marks)
2) What is the writer's purpose: to entertain, to inform and warn, or to advertise a product? Justify.   (2 marks)

III. LANGUAGE - PASSIVE VOICE (6 marks)
1) Put into the passive: "Engineers have already designed more efficient irrigation systems."   (2 marks)
2) Put into the passive: "Scientists must match local efforts with national policies."   (2 marks)
3) Complete the passive: National policies ______ (need) to support long-term investment in renewable energy.   (2 marks)

IV. WRITING - REPORT (4 marks)
Write a short formal report (about 100-120 words) on water management at your school (e.g. leaking taps, waste, awareness). Include a Title, a brief Introduction, one Finding, and one Recommendation, using a formal register.
